title: Galois integral-closure models at generic Cartier DVR stalks
statement: Let N be a locally Noetherian scheme and V an open complement of the image of an integral effective Cartier centre j:D->N. Let eta be a generic point of D, and assume the actual stalk O_{N,j(eta)} is a domain and a discrete valuation ring. Let W be a finite etale Galois cover of a scheme U with finite group G, and let p:P->V be its pullback along kappa:V->U, witnessed by a map r:P->W.P and IsPullback r p W.pi kappa. Assume p is finite etale and its relative normalization over N is finite. For every normalization point x mapping to j(eta), there exist a commutative ring S, a subgroup T of G, an O_{N,j(eta)}-algebra structure on S, and a T-action making S a finite flat domain and IsGaloisGroup T O_{N,j(eta)} S. There is a prime q0 of S whose inertia degree over the same base stalk is the finrank of the canonical residue field extension at x. Scheme, Cartier centre, Galois cover, finite morphism, relative normalization, residue fields, and DVR notions are those of the statement dependencies.

proof.text: The pullback square identifies p with the G-torsor pulled back to V. At the generic point of the integral Cartier centre its stalk is a field, so the localized Cartier ideal is the maximal ideal of the given DVR. Its complement is the fraction field K. Thus the generic algebra is finite etale and carries a simply transitive G-action. Choose the field factor determined by the generization of x and its stabilizer subgroup T. Simple transitivity shows that this factor is a finite Galois extension of K with group T.

Let S be the integral closure of the DVR in the selected field factor. Integral closure commutes with localization, identifying the localized relative normalization with the product of the integral closures of the generic field factors. Finiteness of the relative normalization makes each factor S finite over the base stalk. S is a subring of a field and torsion free over a DVR, hence a flat domain. The stabilizer action preserves integral elements and is faithful. Its invariants belong to K and are integral over the integrally closed DVR, hence are exactly the DVR. This proves IsGaloisGroup T R0 S.

The point x in the localized normalization corresponds to a prime q0 in the selected integral-closure factor. The localization and product comparisons commute with the canonical base maps. Passing to residue fields gives an isomorphism of residue extensions over the identified base residue fields; equality of finranks gives the displayed inertia-degree comparison. No arithmetic degree formula or divisibility theorem is used.

lean.statement:
theorem cartier_generic_stalk_galois_model
    {N U P : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian N]
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G] (W : GaloisCover G U)
    (V : N.Opens) (κ : V.toScheme ⟶ U) (p : P ⟶ V.toScheme) [IsFinite p]
    (r : P ⟶ W.P) (hpb : IsPullback r p W.π κ) :
    let a := p ≫ V.ι
    Etale p → IsFinite a.fromNormalization →
    ∀ (D : Scheme.{u}) (j : D ⟶ N),
      IsIntegral D → IsEffectiveCartierCenter j →
      (∀ z : N, z ∈ V ↔ z ∉ Set.range j) →
      ∀ (η : D), IsGenericPoint η Set.univ →
      ∀ (hdom : IsDomain (N.presheaf.stalk (j η))),
      letI := hdom
      IsDiscreteValuationRing (N.presheaf.stalk (j η)) →
      ∀ (x : a.normalization), a.fromNormalization x = j η →
        ∃ (S : CommRingCat.{u}) (T : Subgroup G)
          (alg : Algebra (N.presheaf.stalk (j η)) S),
          letI := alg
          ∃ (act : MulSemiringAction T S),
          letI := act
          IsDomain (N.presheaf.stalk (j η)) ∧ IsDomain S ∧
          Module.Finite (N.presheaf.stalk (j η)) S ∧
          Module.Flat (N.presheaf.stalk (j η)) S ∧
          IsGaloisGroup T (N.presheaf.stalk (j η)) S ∧
          ∃ (q₀ : Ideal S), q₀.IsPrime ∧
            (letI := (a.fromNormalization.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
             Module.finrank (N.residueField (a.fromNormalization x))
               (a.normalization.residueField x)) = q₀.inertiaDeg (N.presheaf.stalk (j η))
